billing_or_intake_errors.snippet:
Recently had casteel come out to fix an AC issue not cooling. They are Way Overpriced and I feel like not very honest. The first thing the tech told me was that first off you need a thermostat and its not covered under warranty. Reason stated it was not sending low voltage to outside unit.  The price quoted for just the thermostat was 512, for a $150 part. Which means to install the faceplate, 2-3 wires to connect, it was going to cost $372 labor. Took him about 10 minutes to install so you can do the math on the labor rate.  He tried to convince me the cost was high for a 3 yr warranty that they provide. BUT the part comes with a 5 year manufacturer warranty as long as professionally installed. Quality of work was good but way overpriced. Btw in the write up on my receipt, only the faulty transformer was listed as the issue, nothing about the thermostat. Hmmmm. I believe the transformer would be the part that would direct current to the outside unit. So not sure the thermostat was an issue at all

Update: invoice 1003677 Feb 20.  Read back over description, does say faulty thermostat but was tested with faulty transformer. Thermostat was not retested after transformer was replaced

followup_dropped.snippet:
Regretfully, I must change my review. I had my bathtub faucets repaired in March and the tile was broken. Ron was very professional while he was in my home performing the repair but my tile was NEVER replaced.  I have contacted the office several times without any assistance. I keep getting the run around. I was informed that previous supervisor is no longer employed with them. The new supervisor contacted me, I believe his name is Randall, told me that he would get it taken care. But he called me to say that someone was supposed to come look at the tile but they NEVER did. He said he was not informed that they could not come to my home AFTER I called weeks later questioning AGAIN. I have been waiting since March for my bathtub tile to be replaced. Ron placed a heavy duty trash bag along with tape assuring me that it would be replaced. I am wondering when. Now I feel it will never happen. Although, they were efficient with my AC and my hot water heater, I will NEVER use them. If this is how Veterans are treated, I wonder how everyone else is. I am now going to have to pay someone else to fix my tiles. I will no longer do business with AirForce Heating and Air. I recommend others to steer clear!!! I am extremely unsatisfied with the run around and unprofessionalism of their office/employees!!! I am including videos of my bathtub that I emailed to Melissa in June.

I'd previously used AirForce Heating and Air to install an AC unit and  I respected their professionalism and excellent service so I knew who to contact when my hot water heater began leaking water.
Therefore,I sent a request for service through their portal and received a call within an hour. I explained my situation, my hot water heater was totally busted and water was running everywhere! Chris was sent out to evaluate it quickly. He explained that I would definitely need a new hot water heater.
Afterwards, I spoke with Rhett who stated it could be installed the same day if it was delivered before 5 pm. Unfortunately, I could not get it fixed until the very next day.
Ron around promptly the very next morning to install it. He was very professional and helpful throughout the whole process.
I would definitely recommend Airfore Heating and Air!!
followup_dropped.reasoning: Customer has chased a promised tile repair since March, calling repeatedly, and the promised visit never materialized.
followup_dropped.quote: I have contacted the office several times without any assistance

billing_or_intake_errors.snippet:
I wish I could go back in time and never call Swift Bros Plumbing-Heating-Air in Jasper, GA. What a disgusting, greedy, straight-up criminal outfit pretending to be a legit HVAC company. I’m furious and I’m not sugarcoating a damn thing.

They are flat-out scamming customers on every warranty claim. When equipment fails under the manufacturer’s warranty, these crooks quietly pocket the rebate check from the factory, then turn around and bill YOU the full price like it never happened.

I saw it with my own eyes—parts that should’ve been 100% free suddenly get wrapped into "Labor cost" Pure theft.

And their Freon scam is next-level dirty.
They suck the refrigerant out of your old system in some cases (TXV valve replacement in my case), ship it off to get “cleaned and dried,”They then charge you for "FRESH" freon. THEY get a manufacturer rebate when they send your "OLD" freon off to be "Cleaned and Dried",  Meanwhile they’re charging the next customer full price for the exact same gas they just recycled and got paid twice for. Double-dipping on your dime while laughing all the way to the bank.

Their so-called “warranty” is complete and total garbage. They don’t honor one single thing. Everything gets shoved into “labor costs” so they can rip you off without mercy. They wanted over $2,000 for THREE HOURS of work (Mind you all parts were covered under the manufacture warranty).

They take your "warrantied" parts that you paid for and send them back to the manufacture to get a rebate also on them. They never give the customer a single cent of any of the money from any of these rebates, even though the parts are literally belong to the home owner and so therfore does the rebate.

Swift Bros Plumbing-Heating-Air is a predatory, dishonest, money-grabbing scam that preys on regular homeowners who just need their heat or air working. They lie, they cheat, they steal rebates that belong to you, and they hide behind worthless warranties and insane labor gouging.

If you live in Jasper, Ellijay or anywhere nearby, run the other way. Tell every neighbor, every friend, every family member: do not give these crooks a single dime. There are honest HVAC companies out there—Swift Bros is NOT one of them.

Stay far away. You’ve been warned.
billing_or_intake_errors.reasoning: Parts covered under warranty were billed to the customer via inflated labor charges — hidden upcharge/labor gouging.
billing_or_intake_errors.quote: They wanted over $2,000 for THREE HOURS of work

billing_or_intake_errors.snippet:
I called this company out for an HVAC issue and was quoted nearly $950 for a capacitor, hard-start booster, and some wiring repairs. When I declined due to the high price, I was then informed of a $225 emergency service fee that had never been clearly disclosed beforehand. It felt like the fee only became a major issue after I refused the repair. Transparency on pricing is important, and I left the interaction feeling pressured rather than helped.

========= EDIT IN RESPONSE TO OWNER =========

Thank you for the response, but several of these claims need correcting.

I was never told the dollar amount of the emergency rate before your technician arrived. Mentioning "emergency hours" is not the same as disclosing a $225 fee, and I received no written estimate (which i would love to have to show friends) at any point.

No repairs were ever performed and I never gave authorization to proceed. Your own reply states both that "authorization was given to proceed" and that I "declined the quoted repair cost", those can't both be true. Nothing was repaired, because I declined the quote.

I was told my compressor was failing and my capacitor was bad. Neither was true. The system only ever needed the wiring repaired — once that was addressed, it ran fine. The capacitor was good, the compressor was not failing, and the hard-start kit was never necessary. All of it was bundled into a $950 quote on top of what was actually a simple wiring fix.

Those parts run under $50. Even granting professional-grade parts, that gap isn't about quality — it's about it being 4PM on a Sunday. Padding a sub-$50 wiring repair with unneeded parts and a failing-compressor warning, then using emergency timing to push $950, is exactly the pressure I described.

I'll let readers weigh both versions.
billing_or_intake_errors.reasoning: Undisclosed emergency fee surfaced only after the customer declined the repair — classic hidden-charge pain.
billing_or_intake_errors.quote: a $225 emergency service fee that had never been clearly disclosed beforehand
